title: 30006025: reviewed geometric-Chapuy partials; original unsolved (5/5)
body:
## Disposition
Original **30006025 / OWR-14298589-010 remains unsolved after 5/5 substantive author turns**. The full independent source/proof audit passes the scoped results with no mandatory mathematical correction.

The source asks for a geometric adaptation of Chapuy's correspondence in a random-surface comparison. It does not prescribe exact length preservation, algebraic angles, the regular-polygon model or sparse repair. The failures proved here do not exclude every geometric adaptation. The separate volume-identity Question 6 is not silently included.

## Reviewed partials
- Analytic and transcendence obstructions to specified exact-length/equiangular or algebraic-angle prescriptions
- A credited classical regular-polygon/dessin lift to smooth hyperbolic surfaces, with a persistent short-geodesic count-law gap from the source Weil–Petersson comparison
- An angle-independent intrinsic-disk perimeter bound: at curvature −1 a direct one-face realization needs perimeter at least 4π√(g(g−1)), excluding source perimeter 12g for g≥12
- Exact Dirichlet top-k estimates proving that fully adaptive bounded-factor changes on o(g) edges cannot repair that perimeter deficit with nonvanishing probability; a necessary expected-stretch bound without a fixed cap

The cut-disk theorem permits reentrant corners and counts each edge twice. These are necessary results for their precise classes, not sufficiency criteria or a Gromov–Hausdorff impossibility theorem.
